Lines before the first snippet are not assembled.

GNU as creates `.data` before any section the source names, and rsasm creates
it when it is first used. A snippet with both says `.data` first, so the
sections come out in the same order.

Not here: a label as a short direct address (`mov a, label`). The reference
pair disagrees with itself there: GNU as encodes `mov a, 0xffe20` as `8d 20`,
the low byte of the address, which is what the RL78 decodes back to 0xFFE20,
while GNU ld resolves `R_RL78_RH_SADDR` as the address minus 0xFFE20 and
writes `8d 00` for a label there (bfd/elf32-rl78.c), which the CPU reads as
0xFFF00. rsasm writes the low byte in both cases; see tests/rl78.rs.

=== absolute references into another section
        .data
        .text
        movw    ax, #msg
        movw    ax, !msg
        call    !!helper
        call    !helper
        ret
        .data
        .space  0x100
msg:    .word   1
        .section .text.helper, "ax"
helper:
        ret

=== relative calls and branches into another section
        .text
entry:
        call    $!helper
        br      $!helper
        .section .text.helper, "ax"
helper:
        br      $!entry
        ret

=== data across sections
        .text
entry:
        ret
        .data
        .long   entry
        .long   entry - .
        .word   entry
